result.title: CableMoE: Harm-Regularized Mean-Residual Expert Fusion for Transmission-Corridor Segmentation
result.summary: Semantic mapping of transmission corridors benefits from heterogeneous LiDAR and image-guided predictors, but replacing a strong ensemble with a learned router can damage rare electrical assets. We introduce CableMoE, a post-hoc mixture of four frozen segmentation experts. Its deployable prediction is a calibrated residual around availability-aware probability averaging, while a harm penalty discourages extra loss on points that the mean already classifies correctly. A matched component study shows why each design choice is needed: an unconstrained learned mixture loses 1.032 mIoU points relative to probability mean, harm regularization restores 0.359 points at fixed capacity, and removing an unnecessary point-wise gate slightly improves accuracy and stability. With three zones for fitting, two disjoint zones for residual-strength selection, and router-untouched t5b5 for final reporting, CableMoE obtains 84.906% mIoU and 98.140 % overall accuracy. This is +10.000 points over SPT and +0.263 over probability mean; all three seeds improve the latter. Across pylon, conductor, structural-cable, and insulator classes, macro-IoU rises from 84.517% for SPT and 97.153% for probability mean to 98.144 %. The results support conservative residual composition, not a claim of a new segmentation backbone or universal state of the art

AI.brief_summary: 针对输电走廊 LiDAR 与图像分割，提出在四个冻结专家上做后处理式 MoE：预测为可用性感知概率均值附近的校准残差，并用 harm penalty 抑制在均值已判对的点上产生额外损失，最终 mIoU 84.906%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以均值为基线、只加保守残差并以 harm 惩罚保护已正确部分」的融合与监督思路，可能为 LVR 中多路 latent 假设的合并、残差式状态更新及避免新增计算破坏原有正确推理提供可核查线索，但属远距迁移，需判断是否真有对应机制。
